This is a language lesson and must not be presented as allergy or dietary guidance.","Lactose-free milk is cow's milk with the lactose broken down or removed. It still contains milk proteins (casein, whey), so it is a dairy product and is unsafe for someone with a milk-protein allergy. It suits lactose intolerance only.","The source does not say why Tom avoids dairy; his only stated allergy is peanuts. The lactose-free milk in line 9 is Emma's order. Luis asserts it without checking with the kitchen.","Reader line 8 (corn tortillas don't have gluten) is unverified and may be unsafe as stated. Some tortillas are corn-wheat blends, and cross-contact can occur on shared surfaces, presses or fryers.
